summary: Round 8, prose only: no production logic, no wire change, and nothing in this diff adds, moves or authorises an object-store request. Both round-7 findings are genuinely fixed, and I verified each against source rather than against the fix text. (1) The tie-break now has a numbered owner: backlog.md:126 carries criterion 3b -- the event's extent is checked against the RunEntry the same reader fetched and a disagreement refuses rather than decodes -- matching ADR-0044:114-123's 'M5.66 carries the assertion', and it names the silent-failure mechanism correctly: SegmentWriter.encodeRun length-prefixes and CRC32Cs each run block, so a drifted byteStart landing on a neighbouring block passes that block's own CRC and decodes cleanly. (2) The per-byte-term correction is drawn correctly and it is the right distinction. FetchPolicyConfig.java:66 does hold DEFAULT_CROSS_AZ_MICRO_DOLLARS_PER_GB = 20_000L, derivedFrom takes it as a parameter (FetchPolicyConfig.java:104), and the file's own javadoc:22-30 records why it is configuration and not CostTable -- CostTable prices requests and cross-AZ egress is a property of the deployment. What that term prices is EC2 cross-AZ transfer (R12, docs/research/00-problem/02-cost-model.md:299, sourced to ADR-0012), which FetchPolicy.modeFor:70-80 uses to decide whether to ship bytes across an AZ instead of paying the GET they save. It is not an object-store byte price: 02-cost-model.md:29 says bytes between S3 and same-region compute are free and only requests cost money, so a consumer GET on the direct path is in-region free from any AZ. ADR-0044:143-146 and :150-157 say exactly that and withdraw the cross-AZ escape arm, leaving time as the only currency -- correct, and correct more strongly than the record claims, since R12's rate is reachable only on a peer fetch and M5.9 makes a cross-AZ peer unaddressable by construction. The four counted facts under (a), the 5.4%/0.134%/2.46% arithmetic and the sweep table all still hold from round 7 and I did not re-derive them a second time. One minor remains and it must NOT open a round 9 (rule 11): the ADR withdrew the cross-AZ arm, and M5.66's cell still offers it as one of two quantities and still carries the only numbers it has priced on it.

findings.title: ADR-0044 withdrew the cross-AZ currency; M5.66's cell still lists it as a live arm and its only crossover numbers are priced on it
findings.summary: ADR-0044:150-157 now states flatly that R12's $0.02/GB is EC2 cross-AZ traffic, that the bounded read's extra request is an object-store GET whose bytes are in-region free in any AZ, and that 'the only currency left is time'. M5.66's cell got the first half of that correction -- 'THAT TERM PRICES CROSS-AZ TRAFFIC AND NOT THIS PATH ... on dollars alone, in region, the bounded path NEVER wins' -- and then, one clause later, still reads 'The row must therefore say which quantity it is trading: cross-AZ dollars at R12's rate, or TIME'. The arm the record withdrew is still on the row's menu. Worse, every number the row supplies is computed on that arm: 'the bounded path saves 2*objLen/(K+1) - 78,400 against one extra GET (19,968 bytes at R12). Positive to K ~ 169, and on bandwidth alone to K ~ 213 -- both well below ADR-0042's ~400 share, which is why criteria 1 and 2 no longer red each other.' 19,968 bytes per GET IS R12's cross-AZ exchange rate; on the in-region price the row itself now states, a GET buys no bytes at all and the crossover is 0. So after this round the row's reconciliation of criteria 1 and 2 stands on a price the same cell says does not apply, and the currency the ADR leaves standing -- time -- has no derivation anywhere in either document. This is the one-of-two-places shape the row names in its own 3b text, with next-task sending M5.66's owner to the cell before the ADR (the cell says so itself). It is minor, not major: I graded the same substance minor at round 7, the row is strictly better than it was, and criterion 2's independent bounds -- at most two requests at every K, and exactly the whole-object GET at the ~400 share -- hold whatever crossover is recorded, so no request rate is at risk either way.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's owner reads their cell first, as next-task routes them. Criterion 1 tells them to name the price model before measuring; the cell offers 'cross-AZ dollars at R12's rate, or TIME' and then hands them a finished derivation in the first of those -- K ~ 169, with the note that this is why criteria 1 and 2 no longer conflict. They take it, record K ~ 169 in ADR-0044 as criterion 1 requires, and derive the code's threshold from it. The number now sits in a record that says three paragraphs above it that R12's rate prices a path the direct fetch never takes and that the only currency left is time: ADR-0044 contradicts itself on the one figure it declares the single place the number is derived, and the fields are kept on a rate no request on this path incurs. The alternative reading is no better: an owner who follows the ADR instead finds the only currency it admits has no derivation, criterion 2's mandated boundary pair (K = crossover, crossover + 1) has nothing to anchor it, and the in-region dollar answer of 0 selects the removal arm on the price the cell already warns 'nobody argued'.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not open round 9. Record in the commit body, or fold into M5.66 whenever that row is next edited: strike 'cross-AZ dollars at R12's rate, or' from the menu so the row and ADR-0044 agree that time is the only currency, and relabel the K ~ 169 / K ~ 213 arithmetic as what it is -- a bandwidth-versus-one-GET sanity check showing the crossover is below the ~400 share on any plausible exchange rate -- rather than the crossover criterion 1 asks to be measured.
